nodes.name: Four Rails
nodes.description: The four directions of an operation: input (data entering), output (data exiting on success), error (data exiting on failure), trait (character/opinions). Unifies the protocol structure.
nodes.label: four_rails

nodes.name: Operation Model
nodes.description: The fundamental definition: an operation has name, input fields, output fields, and error paths. A fact that exists before transport.
nodes.label: operation_model

nodes.name: Traits as Phenotypes
nodes.description: Biological analogy: operations are genotypes (immutable genetic code), traits are phenotypes (expression in environment). Same genotype produces different traits in HTTP, gRPC, CLI environments.
nodes.label: traits_as_phenotypes

nodes.name: Nine Kinds
nodes.description: The type system: string, integer, float, boolean, binary, datetime, array, object, enum. Derived from physics, not from programming languages.
nodes.label: nine_kinds

nodes.name: Emitter/Receiver
nodes.description: Producer/Consumer pattern. Emitter extracts Instructions from code (Go, PHP, etc). Receiver consumes Instructions and generates artifacts (OpenAPI, code, docs). Share contract, not dependency.
nodes.label: emitter_receiver

nodes.name: Core/Vendor Split
nodes.description: Core is the schema (five fields). Vendors connect by economic gravity. Core is dumb, vendors are smart. Core never changes, opinions live in traits.
nodes.label: core_vendor_split

nodes.name: N×M → N+M Collapse
nodes.description: Without Op: N formats × M tools = N×M bridges. With Op: N emitters + M receivers = N+M, intersections form without glue.
nodes.label: nm_to_nm_collapse

nodes.name: L × M → L + M
nodes.description: Without Op: each program written 1400 times (per vendor/consumer combo). With Op: each program written once per vendor, compiled to all others. Not 1400 copies, one.
nodes.label: lm_collapse

nodes.name: Client Compiler
nodes.description: A thing that did not exist before Op. Not RPC (specific mechanic), not transport, not generator. Reads instruction without knowing transport. Produces typed client.
nodes.label: client_compiler

nodes.name: fn op(instruction, component)
nodes.description: The recurring shape at every layer. Takes declared operation and component that handles some axis. Component reads traits, delegates rest downward. Applied lambda calculus.
nodes.label: fn_op_form

nodes.name: Unix Pipe in Depth
nodes.description: McIlroy's pipe (1964) composed programs linearly. Op turns it 90 degrees: structured typed declarative instruction as contract, tree composition (not linear), inside every component.
nodes.label: unix_pipe_in_depth

nodes.name: Protocol vs Tool vs Library
nodes.description: Protocol: you implement it (SMTP, TCP/IP). Tool: you install it. Library: you import it. Op is a protocol - lives in RFC, not maintained by one author.
nodes.label: protocol_vs_tool

nodes.name: Dumb Protocol Principle
nodes.description: Ousterhout principle: complexity is the enemy. Dumb things live, clever things break (CORBA, WSDL, Smithy). Op is dumb: five fields, all data, no opinions.
nodes.label: dumb_protocol_lives

nodes.name: Fifteen Reinventions
nodes.description: The idea of self-describing operations appeared 15 times in 40 years: D-Bus, UPnP, WSDL, HATEOAS, gRPC Reflection, GraphQL Introspection, MCP, Erlang/OTP, WASI WIT, Plan 9, Tcl, COM, OSGi, Thrift, Toast. Each locked to platform/transport/language.
nodes.label: fifteen_reinventions

nodes.name: Missing UI Format
nodes.description: UI has no universal format (unlike .ttf for fonts, .png for images, .glTF for 3D). Seven frameworks, seven platforms, seven prisons. The empty cell in the format table.
nodes.label: missing_ui_format

nodes.name: Two Layers of Communication
nodes.description: Only two layers exist in any communication: Delivery (TCP/IP, the nervous system) and Meaning (Op, the language). Everything else - HTTP, gRPC, MQTT - is environment, not a layer.
nodes.label: two_layers_communication

nodes.name: SOAP Wound
nodes.description: Industry burned contract together with ceremony. SOAP had WSDL, WS-Security, etc. REST said you don't need any of this, made contract optional. Op separates contract from ceremony.
nodes.label: soap_wound

nodes.name: Man Page Tradition
nodes.description: Dennis Ritchie knew in 1971: every program has a man page. Culture died. Op returns it as economics: /operations is man for the internet, machine-readable, typed.
nodes.label: man_page_tradition

nodes.name: HFT Test
nodes.description: High-frequency trading objection: Op adds latency. Response: Op stands before data, reads once. Blueprint doesn't slow construction. Man page doesn't slow program.
nodes.label: hft_test

nodes.name: Two Layers (1989 Parallel Universe)
nodes.description: In a universe where Op existed before HTTP: URI stays (fact), HTTP becomes trait (opinion), HTML becomes receiver. gRPC, GraphQL, MCP - all phenotypes of one genotype.
nodes.label: two_layers_1989

nodes.name: IP Protocol Field (Enum)
nodes.description: IP's Protocol field (enum at bit 72) is not a data structure - it's a physical address on silicon ASIC. Saved megawatts daily by avoiding modular descriptor system. Enum = switch everywhere.
nodes.label: ip_protocol_field

nodes.name: USB (OCP in Physical World)
nodes.description: USB proved modularity works in hardware. One connector, open container of descriptors. Keyboard, camera, flash drive - one port. USB device descriptor is literally traits.
nodes.label: usb_ocp

nodes.name: Serializability Boundary
nodes.description: Function is not serializable. Channel, file handle, mutex - not serializable. Over the wire only bytes travel. Op describes operations over serializable data - physics, not opinion.
nodes.label: serializability_boundary

nodes.name: Two Plugin Levels
nodes.description: Level 1: Go plugins (typed, import, go/ssa, compile-time). Level 2: External plugins (JSON on stdin, any language). Go plugins can read each other, external plugins are isolated (like Protobuf).
nodes.label: go_plugin_levels

nodes.name: Pipeline vs Isolation
nodes.description: Op Go plugins are a pipeline - httpplug enriches, swagplug reads it. Protobuf plugins are isolated - each gets same model, generates independently, can't read each other.
nodes.label: pipeline_vs_isolation

nodes.name: Traits Are Invariants
nodes.description: A trait is not an annotation - it's a verifiable statement about the call chain. httpplug.Bearer means Authorization header is read and validated. Verify checks via go/ssa call graph.
nodes.label: traits_are_invariants

nodes.name: Zero Runtime Overhead
nodes.description: DSL files carry //go:build op. go build doesn't see them. Op pulls nothing into the binary. Generated code is self-contained. Op is development-time, not runtime.
nodes.label: zero_runtime_overhead

nodes.name: Composable Sets
nodes.description: Traits compose via op.NewSet. Sets can include other sets. Eliminates repetition without coupling. Same pattern as Wire's wire.NewSet.
nodes.label: composable_sets

nodes.name: Three Projections
nodes.description: Verify (check invariants), Generate (code), Describe (structured JSON). All three are plugin-based, not core features. Core provides API, plugins provide expertise.
nodes.label: three_projections

nodes.name: Multi-Module Architecture
nodes.description: One repository: op core, op/httpplug, op/swagplug, op/cobraplug, goop CLI. All share version tag. User imports only what needed. Compatibility guaranteed.
nodes.label: multi_module

nodes.name: Fifteen Times the Same Idea
nodes.description: Devlog #6: The idea that operations should describe themselves has been reinvented fifteen times in forty years. Each time locked to a platform/transport/language.
nodes.label: fifteen_times_same_idea

nodes.name: Go as DSL, Not YAML
nodes.description: Op uses Go as DSL instead of YAML. Go's type system, go/types, go/packages, go/ssa come free. No custom parser, no custom compiler, no custom IDE plugin.
nodes.label: go_as_dsl_not_yaml

nodes.name: Context as Descriptor
nodes.description: op.Tags(ctx) is not descriptor.Tags = append. It's op.AddTag(ctx, posts) - function enriching a build context. Context with typed accessors, not fixed struct.
nodes.label: context_as_descriptor

nodes.name: External Plugin Protocol
nodes.description: JSON on stdin, files on stdout. Same as Protobuf's protoc plugin protocol. Any language can write a plugin. Bidirectional - can enrich model.
nodes.label: external_plugin_protocol

nodes.name: Cross-Language Projections
nodes.description: Model is not Go abstraction - it's abstraction of operation as such. Go is just the IDL language. Projections can target PHP, TypeScript, any language with structs.
nodes.label: cross_language_projections

nodes.name: Tree Topology (Not Graph)
nodes.description: Without Op: graph topology, every node connected to every other (OpenAPI-Protobuf-GraphQL). With Op: tree, Instructions at center, branches outward. Add new node = one branch, not N.
nodes.label: tree_not_graph

nodes.name: No Front Door (Gravity)
nodes.description: Op has no registration, no onboarding. A stranger arrives by naming a URI (vendor), not by asking to join. First outside vendor appeared 40 minutes after #28 published.
nodes.label: no_front_door

nodes.name: Three States of the World
nodes.description: Present: N×M zoo (each program written 1400 times). Transition: extracting from guts (tools forgot self-description). Future: programs know themselves from inside.
nodes.label: three_states_world

nodes.name: AI as Amplifier
nodes.description: Devin AI as intellectual amplifier - signal (insight) in, amplified signal (articulation) out. Same technology as vibe-coding but with signal on input. Long-form thinking failure mode removed.
nodes.label: amplifier_ai

nodes.name: First Stranger (Murat)
nodes.description: First outside vendor: Murat declared urbio/http 40 minutes after devlog #28 published. Evidence, not marketing. Protocol has second orbit.
nodes.label: murat_urbio

nodes.name: Dima (GurovDmitriy)
nodes.description: Saw the four rails - asked why trait is different from input/output/error. Made trait the fourth rail. 56 years after Ritchie split output from error.
nodes.label: dima_four_rails

nodes.name: DeepSeek Cracks
nodes.description: DeepSeek's adversarial review found five cracks: streaming incomplete, impedance mismatch (accepted), Go plugin discrimination, context erosion (accepted), docplug any (accepted). Two splinters remain.
nodes.label: deepseek_cracks

nodes.name: Toast (Dead Tool)
nodes.description: 2019 tool: Go as IDL, plugin architecture. Right idea, wrong execution - tool not protocol. Author left, project died. Protocol lives (SMTP), tool dies.
nodes.label: toast_death

nodes.name: Smithy vs Go Comparison
nodes.description: Smithy built its own world (types, namespace, traits, node values, merge rules, prelude). Go gives all this for free. Smithy has 36 config options to convert to OpenAPI, Op has zero.
nodes.label: smithy_vs_go

nodes.name: gRPC and Protobuf
nodes.description: Protobuf: how (serialization). gRPC: where (transport). Op: what (operation). Protobuf annotations are guests in serialization house, Op traits are owners.
nodes.label: protobuf_grp

nodes.name: HTTP vs Op Address
nodes.description: Berners-Lee 1989: URI is address (fact), HTTP is delivery (opinion), HTML is presentation (opinion). Op fixes first sin: HTTP becomes trait. Second sin remains: no universal UI format.
nodes.label: http_op_address

nodes.name: Fifty Triggers, Fifty Barrels
nodes.description: Modern infrastructure: Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana, OTel, Istio, ArgoCD, Vault, cert-manager - fifty layers, none subtract. The shot (operation) is missing.
nodes.label: fifty_triggers_barrels

nodes.name: What Programs Forgot
nodes.description: Original task: program A calls program B (ARPANET 1969). Forgot: now need HTTP, REST, JSON, OpenAPI, OAuth, CORS to buy a dog. printf didn't abolish assembly, Op doesn't abolish HTTP.
nodes.label: programs_forgot

nodes.description: Memory management (alloc, malloc, page tables, NUMA, OOM) is infrastructure handled by kernel, not application programmers. Same division of labor that kernel provides for memory should exist for other infrastructure layers.
nodes.label: memory_infrastructure

nodes.description: Linus drew the boundary at memory. Application says malloc(size), glibc implements allocator, kernel manages pages, hardware handles cache lines. Four layers, application sees one. The web stack never drew that boundary, leaving applications to manage eight infrastructure axes.
nodes.label: kernel_boundary

nodes.description: Op separates operation (domain) from infrastructure by putting infrastructure in compilers. Application programmer declares, infra engineer maintains the compiler. Same division of labor Linus has with us.
nodes.label: op_boundary

nodes.description: Every program is equal - no built-in category called infrastructure versus application. A business application gets reused by few, a database by many. Reuse is what happened, not what was decided. Equality is the starting point, reuse is the result.
nodes.label: equality_of_programs

nodes.description: When an application talks to a database, it is two programs meeting through their operations. Both have operations, both declare what they do.
nodes.label: database_as_program

nodes.description: git checkout names a state, git handles the transition. High-level languages name variables, compiler picks addresses. JVM HotSpot watches and decides. Database is the last layer where user writes migration plan by hand. The system that owns the state owns the transition.
nodes.label: naming_state_vs_migration_plan

nodes.description: JVM HotSpot is a compiler that runs at runtime. It watches hot paths, recompiles with better assumptions, deoptimises when assumptions break, inlines virtual calls, eliminates allocations through escape analysis. All compilation, not runtime patching.
nodes.label: jit_as_compiler

nodes.description: A compiler can include heuristics, a compiler can include a runtime, a runtime can include a compiler. The static vs runtime split is a limit of older tooling, not of the form.
nodes.label: runtime_compiler

nodes.description: Future op-postgres can observe queries, detect missing indexes, propose schema changes - runtime heuristics inside the compiler, not breaking the form.
nodes.label: op_postgres_runtime

nodes.display_name: Raft as Form that Dissolved Profession
nodes.description: John Ousterhout wrote Raft. Not SRE, not distributed-coordination engineer. Raft is a form. After Raft, thousands of engineers who would have been distributed coordination engineers split into implementation authors and users. The middle dissolved.
nodes.label: raft_form

nodes.description: SRE, Highload engineer, DevOps - same class of word. Names for people holding by hand what the floor above has not yet been written to hold. When the form arrives, labels go, people stay.
nodes.label: disappearing_profession

nodes.description: HotSpot inlines virtual calls, then deoptimises when different type arrives - falls back to slow generic path, recompiles when workload restabilises. Application never knew about the inline or fallback.
nodes.label: jit_deoptimization

nodes.description: Circuit breakers, retry policies, hedge requests, cache stampede protection, fallbacks - every resilience pattern in application is a deoptimisation guard hand-copied from a JIT into source code. The whole resilience playbook is hand-written deopt guards.
nodes.label: hand_written_deopt_guards

nodes.description: A JIT for distributed calls would watch response time histograms, open circuits when latency crosses threshold, race replicas, pin cache fill to single request. Someone will write it. When they do, fifteen years of retry-circuit-cache-fallback ceremony evaporates.
nodes.label: distributed_call_jit

nodes.description: Port in .env, compose.yml, .rr.yaml, Dockerfile, healthcheck, README. Change one, five stay stale. Tools designed in isolation each invent their own config opinion.
nodes.label: config_duplication

nodes.description: envsubst is a second tool whose only job is to paper over the first tool's refusal to interpolate. Adding it admits defeat.
nodes.label: envsubst_workaround

nodes.description: alloc() does one thing. When you need different strategy - dlmalloc, tcmalloc, jemalloc - you switch the allocator, not tune a thousand parameters. Kubernetes does eleven things in one manifest. Real parameterization is printf - tell function what to print, not write formatting logic.
nodes.label: alloc_vs_kubernetes

nodes.description: Five fields exactly - not four (forces attributes, framework wars) not six (welds opinion, competitors add theirs). The count is the peace treaty.
nodes.label: treaty_of_five

nodes.description: When a language drops a field, the unsaid thing moves outside into attributes, decorators, annotations. Spring @Component vs Jakarta @Component. Method wears fifteen attributes from four frameworks. Framework wars begin.
nodes.label: framework_wars

nodes.description: auth, version, transport, serialization, effects, runtime, language, granularity are not core fields. Each refusal is restraint. auth belongs to specific layer; versioning is discipline of evolution over time; transport is the point (transport-agnostic).
nodes.label: non_core_fields

nodes.description: Today choosing database is identity work - We're a Postgres shop, We use Mongo. In a world with clean contract above storage, choice flattens to compiler flag.
nodes.label: database_as_identity

nodes.description: In a world with clean contract above storage, replication becomes flag, sharding becomes flag, multi-region is flag. Migrating is op compile --target=other_storage. The choice that takes quarter and steering committee flattens to benchmark.
nodes.label: storage_compiler_flag

nodes.display_name: Level of Structure as Author Promise
nodes.description: BuyDog(dogId, paymentMethod) -> Receipt is three fields. SQLHTTPProxy.Execute(query string) is one. Both are valid Op operations. Level of structure is author's promise, not Op's requirement. Op refuses the opinion.
nodes.label: promise_level

nodes.description: HTTP shows same shape - Content-Type: JSON Schema promises exact body, text/plain promises text, octet-stream promises bytes. HTTP does not have opinion which to pick. Op is same shape one floor up.
nodes.label: http_content_type_analogy

nodes.description: Smithy pushes toward fine structuring, gRPC requires typed messages, OpenAPI rewards JSON Schema, WSDL made not-structuring embarrassing. Each has default opinion reinforced by tooling.
nodes.label: granularity_pushback

nodes.description: When debugging high-level code, we don't pick variable addresses - compiler does. URLs are the same kind of detail one floor up. Human reads operation, compiler picks URLs or gRPC or queue.
nodes.label: urls_as_wire_binding

nodes.description: When humans stop reading URLs, REST dies not because Op forbids it - REST dies because humans looking at URLs was the only reason for special status. REST becomes trait under http/*.
nodes.label: rest_becomes_binding

nodes.description: PHP frameworks are built for production day one. Two hours bootstrap before single line of emitter logic. Laravel, Symfony, Spiral all assume deploying from minute one.
nodes.label: php_framework_pain

nodes.description: Cloud platforms promise write-a-function, infrastructure hidden. Price is SDK - once shaped to one cloud's API, leaving is rewrite. Lock is in rewrite cost, not bill.
nodes.label: cloud_sdk_lock

nodes.description: With portable contract above all clouds, Lambda, Workers, Machines all read same instruction. Each compiles to own runtime. Application shaped to its operations, cloud is one compiler away.
nodes.label: portable_contract

nodes.description: Mongo is a program; Op is a contract. Different layer. Protocol gets sold to market, becomes product. Protocol stays neutral, stays protocol.
nodes.label: program_vs_contract

nodes.description: Postgres is a program. Linux kernel is a program. Browser, calculator, GPT-4, music box, traffic light, coffee maker, sewer plumbing, wheat farm, DNA replication, brain, universe - all accept input, return output, can fail. Same protocol, different authors, goals, scales.
nodes.label: all_programs_equal

nodes.description: Five fields describe shape of interaction itself. Interaction does not care whether parties are silicon, neurons, hyphae, or planetary motion. The form is universal.
nodes.label: interaction_shape

nodes.description: Browser fires connections to multiple IPs in parallel, first to respond wins. Hedging, speculative concurrency. CLI tools never had the contract for this.
nodes.label: happy_eyeballs

nodes.description: In Op, hedging is just a component. trait: hedge/parallel: 3. Any client gets hedging for free, whether it knows about hedging or not.
nodes.label: hedge_trait

nodes.description: Cloud portability and AI callability are markets that would benefit if Op succeeded. Temptation is the trap - protocols sold to markets die as protocols, survive as products.
nodes.label: hungry_markets

nodes.description: WSDL sold to enterprise IT became enterprise software. OpenAPI kept neutral stayed protocol. Day Op starts performing for a market,Op stops being form, becomes feature of company.
nodes.label: protocol_vs_product_trap

nodes.description: Postgres is not database - it is bundle. Storage engine, B-tree, MVCC, WAL, planner, statistics, vacuum, replication welded together. No contract existed to make smaller unit.
nodes.label: postgres_bundle

nodes.description: SQLite ships as storage engine. DuckDB took columnar OLAP. CockroachDB took Raft. Each single component pulled out, shipped, bundle leaked. What missing is form/contract.
nodes.label: unbundling_already_happening

nodes.description: Postgres is virtual machine with JIT, profiler, inline cache, garbage collector. Statistics collector = profiler, planner = optimizing compiler, EXPLAIN ANALYZE = bytecode inspector, plan cache = inline cache, auto-vacuum = GC. SQL is bytecode.
nodes.label: postgres_jit

nodes.description: ORM is translator between two VMs. Class definitions to SQL, methods to queries, types to types. ORM is literally cross-compiler between two VMs never designed to know each other.
nodes.label: orm_as_cross_compiler

nodes.description: Minimum has two properties - cannot be attacked for excess (every field carries falsifiable claim), cannot be attacked for absence (by construction, found by removing until removing next would break). There is nothing to break.
nodes.label: primitive_invulnerability

nodes.description: Attacks reduce to small classes: just another OpenAPI, static compiler can't heuristics, takes away transparency, compares to predecessors, AI wrote it, security risk, manifesto, compiler can't handle queries, what about latest thing, nobody needs this. Each maps to prior responses.
nodes.label: attack_patterns

nodes.description: RoadRunner .rr.yaml has four concerns in one file - transport, process management, domain middleware, infrastructure observability. No boundaries. Layers welded where should slide.
nodes.label: layers_welded_shut

nodes.description: http address, server command, logs level, metrics address - five different professions smashed into one file, no schema explaining which line answers which question.
nodes.label: four_concerns_one_file

nodes.description: A unit of work with input, output, and error. Defined as: operation = takes × gives × can break
nodes.label: operation

nodes.description: Design principle: need comes before form. First the desire, then the form that serves it. Never the reverse
nodes.label: need_first_principle

nodes.description: Agreement through the smallest common denominator, not opinion. Like the handle on a faucet - minimal form that all can agree to
nodes.label: smallest_common

nodes.description: Sound is fact (mouth, throat, air universal). Letter is form (language opinion). Writing records sound, not meaning
nodes.label: sound_is_fact

nodes.description: A cover without title or color - removes all opinion so nothing repels. Black is when all colors are removed, so it does not conflict
nodes.label: black_cover

nodes.description: Simulation algorithm using three rules: separation, alignment, cohesion. No leader, no map, no plan. Six neighbors is sufficient
nodes.label: boids

nodes.description: Flock of starlings performing synchronized turns. Uses topological interaction - counts nearest neighbors not distance. Three rules produce emergent sky
nodes.label: murmuration

nodes.description: Bee communication: angle=direction relative to sun, duration=distance (~750m/sec), vigour=quality. Three parameters, thirty million years working
nodes.label: waggle_dance

nodes.description: The edge where travelling thing meets resting thing. Agreement at the edge enables enormous trade. Small agreement, large enablement
nodes.label: harbourmaster

nodes.description: A form so small it carries no opinion, so complete it describes itself. Makes room for viewer to bring their own meaning
nodes.label: black_square

nodes.description: A form that carries no opinion, admits every reading. Does not tell viewer what to see - tells viewer seeing is possible
nodes.label: primitive

nodes.description: Capability declaration: here is what I can do. Small, self-describing, carries no opinion about reader. Reader reads what it needs
nodes.label: menu

nodes.description: The minimal act of recognition combining id (machine name) and comment (human meaning). The wrapper is the same as what it wraps
nodes.label: nota

nodes.description: Five fields exactly: id, comment, input, output, error. Fewer escapes to attributes (war), moreWelds opinion in core (war). Number is the pact
nodes.label: five_fields_treaty

nodes.description: Resilience pattern hand-copied from JIT to application code: circuit breaker, retry, hedge, cache fill. Pattern lives in wrong place - needs JIT above calls
nodes.label: deopt_guard

nodes.description: Last layer where naming state is not enough. Git, compilers crossed this line. Database has not. Plan should be internal
nodes.label: migration

nodes.description: Boundary drawn at right abstraction - app programmer declares, kernel maintains. Same as Linus has with us. The web stack never drew it
nodes.label: allocation_boundary

nodes.description: Config lives in .env, compose.yml, .rr.yaml, Dockerfile, proxy, README. One change, five stay stale. Tools invent own config opinions
nodes.label: single_source_truth

nodes.description: alloc() does one thing. Switch allocators, not tune parameters. k8s does eleven things - one manifest. 100-parameter config is admission no one knows answer
nodes.label: configuration_not_parameterization

nodes.description: Runtime compiler that picks its moment - watches hot paths, recompiles with better assumptions, deoptimizes when broken
nodes.label: jvm_hotspot

nodes.description: Modern infrastructure: K8s, Helm, Terraform, Prometheus, Istio, ArgoCD, Vault, cert-manager. Every layer added, none subtracted. Shape of shot never written
nodes.label: fifty_triggers_fifty_barrels

nodes.description: The bound book: cover, title, page numbers, index made knowledge addressable. Turned scroll (stream) into place. Gave identity to content
nodes.label: codex

nodes.description: Program without instruction cannot be invoked. Instruction without program has nothing to invoke. Neither viable alone
nodes.label: program_instruction_mutual_dependency

nodes.description: Program to program communication. 1969 ARPANET, 1971 FTP. TCP, HTTP, REST, JSON are layers. Fifty years became wall between programmer and goal
nodes.label: original_task

nodes.description: Op pushes layers below where they belong. go-http-client knows TLS, op-retry knows 429. Programmer sees op(BuyDog)
nodes.label: op_pushes_layers_down
